newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stocks end weak as properties continue slide.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks end weak as properties continue slide.

text.p: Hong Kong property stocks took another hit on Friday, dragging the Hang Seng Index to a lower close, with a fresh slide in Japanese stocks also weighing on sentiment, brokers said.
The blue-chip index fell 6.61 points, or 0.05 percent, to 13,191.50. Turnover was HK$11.33 billion compared with HK$11.41 billion on Thursday.

"Tokyo falling down put a few jitters among investors and sent them towards the sidelines where concern over action over property speculation meant that we have seen a gradual selloff," said Miles Remington, sales trader at SocGen-Crosby Securities.
In Japan, the Nikkei 225 tumbled 770.22 points, or 4.26 percent, to 17,303.65.

This week, the Hang Seng Index slipped 31.29 points or 0.24 percent. Analysts said speculation has been mounting that the Hong Kong government may impose measures, possibly as early as next week, to curb escalating prices in the property market.

"Most of the drop in the Hang Seng comes from the property counters, which is because of concerns over an interest rate increase (in the United States) and the announcement by the government that they might impose measures in the property market," said ImPac Asset Management analyst Kelvin Tang.

Shares in Cheung Kong fell HK$1.00 to HK$71.25 and Sun Hung Kai Properties shed HK$1.00 to HK$91.25. Henderson Land fell HK$0.75 to HK$72.25, New World Development dropped HK$1.00 to HK$50.25 and Swire Pacific slumped HK$1.25 to HK$70.75.

"There are still a lot of investors staying on the sidelines waiting for next week's announcement on measures to clamp down on speculation in the property market and today's (U.S.) jobs figures," said Patrick Chia, research director at China Everbright Research.
U.S. December employment data are due later on Friday.
But shares in Hongkong Telecom gained HK$0.50 to HK$13.30 on renewed speculation that parent Cable and Wireless Plc may sell a stake in the company.
Brokers said market talk that C&W could sell part of its 59 percent stake to Singapore Telecommunications boosted sentiment. Singtel denied it was seeking to buy a stake from C&W.
HSBC Holdings was also a winner on Friday, rising HK$2.50 to HK$168.00.
"People have been switching into banks as well as utilities, being perceived as defensive plays," said Remington.
